evidence.quote: At this school, students are randomly assigned to classrooms (with the exception of honors-designated classrooms, which we exclude from our main sample). We assigned each classroom to one of three treatment arms—control, GPT Base, and GPT Tutor.# The control arm is business-as-usual, having students work through the practice problems with access to course books and notes with no devices provided. evidence.quote: Finally, while our study takes a step toward understanding the potential harms of generative AI on learning, it focuses on a specific deployment context, and substantial work is needed to better understand the nature and scope of these effects. First, our study focuses on two generative AI tutors for a single topic (mathematics) deployed in a single high school in Turkey. We have objective evaluation criteria for math problems, which is unavailable in other important subjects such as writing. Our deployment was also carried out in Fall 2023, when generative AI was still very new; modes of interaction may have changed now that users are more familiar with effective uses of these tools and their shortcomings. Furthermore, both closed and open-weight models have significantly improved in performance since then. Additional studies are required to assess generalizability to other tutor designs and deployment contexts. Moreover, we focus on short-term outcomes due to limitations imposed by our partner school; studying long-term outcomes is a key direction for future research. Last, while we have performed several analyses to uncover mechanisms underlying our findings, our approach can be complemented with controlled experiments in settings where more fine-grained interventions and monitoring are possible to better understand these mechanisms.

evidence.quote: Table 1 reports intention-to-treat estimates from this regression. We find that GPT Base and GPT Tutor substantially increased student scores in the GPT-assisted practice sessions by 0.137 and 0.361 (out of 1), respectively, relative to the control arm that only had access to textbooks (mean performance of 0.28). These results imply that GPT Base and GPT Tutor would increase performance on the assisted practice sessions by 48% and 127%, respectively, on average relative to the control arm. These results are consistent with the existing literature on the productivity effects of generative AI (7, 8). Furthermore, the gap between GPT Tutor and GPT Base illustrates the added benefits of problem-specific teacher inputs in the prompt. Specifically, GPT Base often provides incorrect answers due to hallucinations; in contrast, the prompt for GPT Tutor includes the solution along with recommended hints, which enables students to both obtain useful hints and check their answers once they have them. Our mechanism analysis in the next section provides a more detailed analysis supporting this hypothesis.

evidence.quote: In stark contrast, in the subsequent unassisted exam, student performance in the GPT Base arm degraded by 0.054 (out of 1) relative to that of the control arm. In other words, GPT Base diminished the average control student’s performance on the unassisted exam by 17%. Student performance in the GPT Tutor arm was statistically indistinguishable from that of the control arm, and the point estimate was smaller by an order of magnitude (−0.004). The fact that students in the GPT Tutor arm performed similarly to students in the control arm on the unassisted exam may be surprising since they performed so much better on the practice problems. answer.text: In the study's assisted practice sessions, both GPT Base and GPT Tutor outperformed the control group. In the unassisted exam, GPT Base performed worse than the control group; the difference between GPT Tutor and the control group was not statistically significant. These results reflect different testing conditions. Practice scores alone cannot establish independent learning.

The authors describe a specific deployment context: mathematics teaching in a single school, with short-term outcomes. The selected passages do not establish improvements or harms in long-term retention or transfer to unfamiliar tasks. They also do not establish a particular dependency mechanism as the confirmed cause of the results.

answer.text: During assisted practice sessions, both GPT-based tutoring tools substantially boosted student performance relative to control (textbooks only). GPT Tutor showed larger gains than GPT Base, possibly because its prompts included teacher-vetted solutions and hints, whereas GPT Base sometimes provided incorrect answers due to hallucinations.

On a subsequent unaided exam, GPT Base performance degraded relative to control. GPT Tutor performance on the unaided exam was statistically indistinguishable from control, despite much stronger assisted practice gains. Long-term retention and transfer to unfamiliar tasks remain unknown from these passages.

student.text: When given AI tutoring help during practice, students scored much better. But when tested without help afterward, the basic AI tool actually hurt performance, while the smarter tutored version did about the same as learning from books alone—showing that doing well with help doesn't automatically mean doing well on your own.

educator.text: This RCT distinguishes assisted practice (with tool access) from unaided performance (exam without tools). Enhanced practice did not transfer; GPT Base harmed exam scores, and GPT Tutor showed no significant exam gain despite large practice improvements. This suggests over-reliance on checking answers during practice may reduce independent problem-solving, though the mechanism remains hypothetical.

professional.text: The study evaluates a single high school in Turkey during Fall 2023 and measures only short-term outcomes (assisted sessions and a subsequent exam). Generalizability across schools, subjects, AI model versions, and user expertise is limited. Long-term retention and transfer effects were not measured due to school constraints, leaving critical questions about sustained learning impact unanswered.
